report_name: Winona County, MN Paid Ransom Before Being Hit a Second Time

threat_actors.name: January 2026 Winona County Attacker
threat_actors.description: The unidentified ransomware group that conducted the first attack against Winona County in January 2026, successfully extorting a ransom of $128,539 after stealing resident data.

threat_actors.name: April 2026 Winona County Attacker
threat_actors.description: The second, unrelated ransomware group that attacked Winona County in April 2026, three months after the first incident, causing further significant disruption.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware was deployed to encrypt systems in Winona County in two separate attacks, disrupting services and leading to a ransom payment in the first incident.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Attackers in the January 2026 incident stole data containing names, Social Security numbers, and medical information before deploying ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely deleted Volume Shadow Copies to prevent easy system recovery, a common ransomware precursor technique suggested for detection via 'vssadmin delete shadows' commands.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: The attackers likely performed credential harvesting using tools like Mimikatz to gain broader access to the network, a behavior suggested for hunting by the report.

identities.name: Winona County
identities.description: A county in Minnesota that was the victim of two separate ransomware attacks in January and April 2026, and paid a $128,539 ransom after the first attack.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8a1c3d-e4f5-4a9b-8cde-f1234567890a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware deployment.
references:
  - https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/09/06/winona-county-attacked-again-in-cyberattack-after-paying-128-ransom
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-06
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a technique often used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: Mimikatz Credential Dumping Tool Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Mimikatz Execution Detection
id: 9f8b7c6d-5a4b-4c3d-b2a1-0987654321fe
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of Mimikatz, a common tool for credential dumping, as suggested by hunting hints for ransomware intrusions.
references:
  - https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/09/06/winona-county-attacked-again-in-cyberattack-after-paying-128-ransom
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-06
tags:
  - attack.t1003
  - attack.credential_access
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    - Image|endswith: '\mimikatz.exe'
    - OriginalFileName: 'mimikatz.exe'
    - CommandLine|contains: 'mimikatz'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the credential dumping tool Mimikatz, a strong indicator of an active intrusion.
